pr_title: feat: added reduced motion media query emulation

issue_context.title: [Feature] Emulate reduced motion media query
issue_context.body:
Puppeteer allows emulating the reduced motion media query: https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/v5.2.1/docs/api.md#pageemulatemediafeaturesfeatures

It would be great if we can support this in playwright as well. It's widely supported in browsers: https://caniuse.com/#feat=prefers-reduced-motion
comments: Could you help us prioritizing this? Does it come from a customer or is it a feature parity request?

It's about feature parity. It's same story as https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/3321 - we offer bindings for emulating media features from tests, using both puppeteer and playwright. Right now we throw an error when trying to emulate reduced motion when running tests with playwright.

This would be incredibly useful for testing purposes. For accessibility purposes, we disable all animations based the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.

Being able to set it to avoid fragile tests would save a bunch of time overall!

FWIW I'd like to be able to emulate this media query so I don't have to wait for animations to end in my tests. Of course something like https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/4055 would help as well but without either I'm just doing arbitrary `page.waitForTimeout`s all over the place haha

review_comments: Let's have a test for default behavior, if we decide to not fallback to system default.
Just match `no-preference` before the first `emulateMedia` call.
How does this reset to system default? Or do we always want 'no-preference' by default?

Passing null should reset it to system defaults. Hard to test since browsers implement the detection differently, some do it only for windows and some not.
I will test it and keep you updated.
It is safe to drop these checks, client should take care of it. And if it does not, protocol validator will yell anyway.
Not sure what you mean with the last question.My point is that we can remove lines 365-370 in the new code, and all tests will still pass.
